successors.note: The Hafsid dossier has Abu Faris annex Tripoli in 1401 with the counterpart 'nobody'.

capitals.name: Tripoli
capitals.note: The page has the family 'ruled Tripoli' in the 14th century; the city is also the only place it names.

correction.text: Tripoli, taken over by Thabit ibn 'Ammar 'toward 1324', governed 'nominally on behalf of the Hafsids' but 'effectively independent of Tunis'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page names Tripoli only and gives no area. The 50 km circle is the researcher's; Cliopatria has no row for Tripolitania before the Hafsid shapes of 1236, which carry it throughout, so this is the overlap to correct (Hafsid dossier, note 2).

correction.text: Tripoli, retaken by Abu Bakr in 1369-1370 from the Banu Makki to whom the Genoese had given it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The Genoese capture of Tripoli came in 1354-1355'; 'retaking the city took place in 1369-1370'. The years 1354-1368 have no shape: the Genoese and then the Banu Makki hold the city.

ledger.note: c. 1324: Thabit ibn 'Ammar takes power in Tripoli. He 'took power in the city toward 1324' and was murdered six months later; Muhammad's command began in 1326-1327, 'when the local population gave him control of the city'. The family governed 'nominally on behalf of the Hafsids' (Tripoli came under Hafsid authority after the Almohad collapse in the early 13th century). [Reviewer af-02-x: counterpart hafsid-dynasty, not nobody: the page has Thabit seize power after a rebellion expelled the Hafsid governor Ibn Abi 'Umran, appointed by Abu Yahya Abu Bakr II.]

1354-55: the Genoese capture Tripoli. 'The Genoese capture of Tripoli came in 1354-1355'; Thabit (Muhammad's son) and his brother were killed by the Awlad Margham in 1354-1355, and 'the Genoese agreed to give the city to the Banu Makki, the rulers of Gabès' in exchange for a large payment.
1369-70: Abu Bakr retakes Tripoli. The brother of the murdered Thabit 'retook the city in 1369-1370' and died in 1389-1390; Ali, his nephew, succeeded him.

1401: the Hafsids take Tripoli. The Hafsid attack of 1392-1393 failed; Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz II arrested Ali in 1397-1398 and installed Yahya and 'Abd al-Wahid; 'He returned and finally captured the city in 1401'. 'Their rule definitely ended with the Hafsid reconquest of the city in 1401.'
1401: the dynasty ends. 'Their rule definitely ended with the Hafsid reconquest of the city in 1401.'

wars.name: Genoese capture of Tripoli
wars.outcome: The Genoese captured Tripoli in 1354-1355; Thabit and his brother were killed by the Awlad Margham; the Genoese gave the city to the Banu Makki of Gabès for a large payment.
wars.note: The page gives no day for the capture.

wars.name: Banu Thabit against the Banu Makki
Hafsid campaigns against Tripoli
wars.outcome: The Hafsid attack of 1392-1393 failed, with some Arab tribal support; Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz II arrested Ali in 1397-1398; the Hafsids captured the city in 1401.

certainty.note: The page names Tripoli only; the 50 km circle is the researcher's, and 1354-1368 has no shape.

notes: Cliopatria has no Banu Thabit row; its Hafsid Dynasty row carries Tripolitania from 1236. The Hafsid dossier records Abu Faris's 1401 annexation of Tripoli with the counterpart 'nobody' because no page named the holder; this dossier supplies it. The Banu Makki page says their domain 'extended from Gabès to Tripoli' at its height 'sometime the early 14th century', which conflicts with this page's rule of Tripoli from c. 1324 and is left to the Banu Makki dossier's notes. Regnal years on the page are given as year pairs (1326-1327 for Muhammad's command, 1348 for his murder, 1354-1355 and 1369-1370, 1389-1390, 1397-1398); the first of each pair is used. The page has no infobox, so no area or dates were compared.
